abstract.p: A method for pretreating metal sheets to be painted, the particularity of which consists of the fact that degreasing and phosphating of the metal sheets are performed simultaneously in a single step, assisting the chemical action of a degreasing-phosphating solution with the application of mechanical energy.

L'invention porte sur un procédé de prétraitement de plaques métalliques à peindre, la particularité de ce procédé consistant à dégraisser et phosphater simultanément les plaques métalliques en une seule étape, et faciliter l'action chimique d'une solution de dégraissage-phosphatation par application d'une énergie mécanique.

DESCRIPTION
The present invention relates to a method for pretreating metal sheets to be painted.
It is known that metal sheets used for the production of many components, such as panels of

such as washing machines or air conditioners, require treatment processes as a preliminary to painting, so as to bring the surface to the best conditions to allow optimum adhesion of the
paint.
In the cm rent state of the art, a typical treatment for preparing the metal sheet for painting

mainly entails peitorming degreasing, in order to eliminate solid particles, residues of rolling- mill oils and other contaminants, and phosphating (conversion) in order to form a layer of phosphor salts on the surface of the sheets; these salts facilitate the adhesion of the paint and
provide protection against corrosion.
In conventional-type treatments, degreasing and phosphating are performed in separate and
mutually successive steps with the addition of intermediate and final rinses. For example, one

or zinc phosphate (pH 2.8), (also known as phosphating), and two rinses, the latter using
demineiahzed water. The overall duration of a treatment of this type for die-cut metal sheets
is approximately 10 minutes.

claim.claim-text: CLAIMS
1. A method for pretreating metal sheets to be painted, characterized in that it comprises
the steps of: a) simultaneous degreasing and phosphating the metal sheets by means of the chemical
action of a degreasing and phosphating solution assisted by the application of mechanical energy;
b) final rinsing of said metal sheets.
2. The method according to claim 1 , characterized in that said step a) is provided by high-
pressure spraying of said degreasing and phosphating solution.
3. The method according to claim 2, characterized in that abrasive powders or polymeric
powders or glass beads are added to said degreasing and phosphating solution.
4. The method according to one or more of the preceding claims, characterized in that said
degreasing and phosphating solution comprises a surfactant.
5. The method according to one or more of the preceding claims, characterized in that said
degreasing and phosphating solution furthermore comprises zinc oxides and/or salts,
and/or iron oxides and/or salts, and phosphoric acid and/or derivatives thereof.
6. The method according to one or more of the preceding claims, characterized in that said degreasing and phosphating solution is sprayed at a pressure between 3 and 80 bar,
preferably between 5 and 60 bar, more preferably between 10 and 30 bar.
7. The method according to one or more of the preceding claims, characterized in that said
degreasing and phosphating solution has a temperature which can vary between 30 and
80°C. preferably between 40 and 70°C, more preferably between 50 and 60°C.
8. The method according to claim 1 , characterized in that said step a) is performed by using ultrasonic waves.

9. The method according to one or more of the preceding claims, characterized in that it
compiises a predegreasing step before said step a).
10 The method according to one or more of the preceding claims, characterized in that said step b) is performed in deminerahzed water at ambient temperature and pressure.
1 1 The method accoiding to one oi more of claims 1 to 9, characterized in that said step b) is pei foi med in deminerahzed water at ambient temperature and at high pressure.
12. The method according to claim 1 , characterized in that said metal sheets comprise die- cut, drawn or pie-folded metal sheets.
